# Belgian PKCS#11 source and replacement

The selected DLL is the unchanged vendor-signed 5.2.0.6426 x64 DLL extracted
from the official-hosted test wrapper 5.2.0.6447. The source snapshot installed
as `licenses/Belgian-eID-source.zip` is the corresponding source identified by
the owner's report of confirmation from Thomas Charlier at Zetes. It contains the unmodified
upstream tree at `5abf0ca70280320e79371faf207f427e1b852b1b` plus the version
header generated by upstream's script for revision count 6426. The archive
includes COPYING, source copyright notices, build projects, resource files,
bundled LibTomCrypt hash implementations and OASIS PKCS#11 headers.

`MIDDLEWARE-PROVENANCE.json` records the selected vendor DLL and corresponding
source/archive hashes, with the evidence classification. A successful independent
build demonstrates that the public source is buildable. The vendor source
mapping is recorded separately with its evidence scope; the original correspondence
was not independently reviewed. The build uses Visual Studio 2022's
v143 C++ toolset and Windows SDK. Microsoft OS/compiler libraries are separate
system/compiler dependencies, not missing proprietary middleware source.

## Rebuild from the included archive

1. Extract the ZIP to a writable directory. Preserve its `eid-mw` tree, including
   `scripts/windows/beidversions.h`; the pre-generated header permits an offline
   build without Git history or regenerating version numbers.
2. Install a validly licensed Visual Studio 2022 edition with Desktop development
   with C++ and a Windows 10/11 SDK. Free Community is an option for eligible
   open-source development. Open its x64 Native Tools command prompt.
3. From the extracted `eid-mw` directory, run:

   ```bat
   msbuild cardcomm\pkcs11\VS_2022\beidpkcs11.vcxproj /m /p:Configuration=Release /p:Platform=x64
   ```

4. The output is `cardcomm/pkcs11/VS_2022/Binaries/x64_Release/beidpkcs11.dll`.
   Compiler/SDK versions and normal PE build timestamps may cause different
   binary hashes. A byte-identical build is not asserted.

For a fresh Git build, clone <https://github.com/Fedict/eid-mw>, check out the
exact SHA with complete history, run `scripts/windows/create_eidmw_version_files.cmd`
to generate the version header, and use the same MSBuild command. Our build
helper and pinned CI workflow are in the bridge source repository.

## Library replacement

The bridge dynamically loads `beidpkcs11.dll` from its application directory.
There is no application-time middleware hash or signature lock. A user can
replace it with a compatible modified x64 library with the same PKCS#11 exports.
Close the bridge first, retain a backup, and use administrator access to replace
the DLL under `C:\Program Files\LetsPeppol eID Bridge`. Retain licence notices.
Install/repair/upgrade may restore packaged files; keep modifications separately.
The LGPL permits debugging library modifications and governs this library
independently of the MIT application. Windows execution policies still apply.

The selected packaged DLL retains its original ZETES signature. Independently
built comparison DLLs are not substituted for it. Neither source availability
nor a vendor signature implies Belgian government endorsement or production
approval of this bridge or of the upstream test build.
